title: Identifying Population Intervention Laws from Experiments with Post-Treatment Selection on Trees
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded subfield below the required field floor; math panel passed after local repairs, with Bareinboim--Tian theorem-level comparison still unresolved.
gap_reasons: The broader sparse-menu problem advertised as the practically relevant extension remains open: the forest-potential construction is only an ansatz and supplies neither complete elimination nor complexity or rational-witness guarantees.
paper_score_ceiling 7.1 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.

Add and compare Bareinboim--Tian (AAAI 2015), which gives graphical/algorithmic recoverability conditions and a Markovian completeness claim for causal effects under selection bias; explain at theorem level why its selected-law setting neither yields nor is implied by the normalized post-intervention multi-arm fiber and saturation equivalence here.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived an exact saturation-menu fiber characterization, target-invariance criterion with twins, and fixed-design recruitment-denominator count on positive finite rooted trees. Two localized math findings were repaired and the final math panel passed with no findings. D0.5 graded the delivered package subfield below the field floor because complete sparse-menu elimination, joint-denominator constraints, complexity, and corresponding twins remain open; the Bareinboim--Tian theorem-level comparison also remains an explicit positioning gap.
tldr: Every experiment may be randomized correctly yet reveal only units recruited after treatment, so even an unlimited collection of normalized selected arms can conceal population intervention laws. On positive finite rooted trees, the selection-local saturation menu consists only of the selected observational law and single-node arms on nonroot selector parents. The selected observational law together with single-node arms on nonroot selector parents is information-saturating: its compatible-model fiber is parameterized by independent local normalization gauges and equals the fiber induced by the full collection of normalized hard-intervention laws. Cross-arm ratios evaluated at the intervention state are invariant to all remaining table coordinates and reconstruct every other mechanism. A canonical positive reconstruction makes the typed path coefficient-span test fully observable, giving a necessary-and-sufficient target criterion and, for rational supplied selected-law tables and recruitment denominators, positive rational twins on failure. With the observational recruitment probability measured, the exact number of extra single-arm denominators required to recover every mechanism is the sum of observable local nullities. For sparse menus, an induced-selector-forest potential ansatz and cut-product constraints provide a concrete starting point; sound-and-complete elimination, complexity, and rational-twin guarantees remain open.
gap: Selected-experiment adjustment, general do-calculus search, unselected gID, and context-selected data fusion do not characterize the cross-arm model fiber created when the same endogenous selector is realized after every intervention and each arm is normalized separately.
fill: The project delivers an exact saturation fiber, coordinate-invariant observable ratios, a canonical positive reconstruction, a fully typed law-specific causal-target iff with constructive twins, and a sharp fixed-design denominator count, while isolating sparse forest-potential elimination as the genuine open extension.
